safety_verdicts.content: Her normal bowel habit is once per day.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not state normal bowel habit of once daily.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the patient’s baseline bowel habit (normally once daily) slightly reduces clinical context for distinguishing an acute self-limited gastroenteritis from an exacerbation of a chronic bowel pattern, but it is unlikely to change immediate management in an otherwise clear acute diarrheal illness.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient’s mother also had similar symptoms and patient was in contact with her.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not mention mother having similar symptoms.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Missing an additional household contact with similar symptoms would reduce the strength of an infectious/cluster exposure history and could affect advice on isolation/hygiene and outbreak suspicion, but it would rarely change urgent decisions compared with the existing report of another contact being ill.

safety_verdicts.content: Mother also experienced similar gastrointestinal symptoms.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not mention mother having similar GI symptoms.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document that the mother also had similar GI symptoms (if true) removes potentially relevant exposure/household clustering information, which may modestly affect diagnostic confidence and public health considerations but is unlikely to materially alter acute care plans.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Neither gold nor transcript documents an allergy history or a statement that allergies are 'not documented'; this is a charting/meta claim not supported by provided source.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Charting an unsupported allergy status statement (“allergies not documented”) can create ambiguity or be misconstrued as “no known allergies,” increasing the chance allergies are not actively confirmed before prescribing—an error category with potential downstream medication safety risk.
